evidence_timeline.summary: A spectrum was taken with the Nordic Optical Telescope (NOT) of the transient AT 2026yos, which was highlighted as a potential kilonova candidate by Gillanders et al. (AstroNote 2026-245). Our spectrum shows Hydrogen and Helium narrow emission lines at z = 0, identifying AT 2026yos as a Galactic object instead, likely a CV.

evidence_timeline.summary: We report multiband photometric follow-up observations of AT 2026yos (ATLAS26jvy), a rapidly fading transient discovered by ATLAS (Gillanders et al., AstroNote 2026-245). We observed the transient with the Lulin One-meter Telescope (LOT) at Lulin Observatory beginning at MJD 61264.566, approximately 1.64 days after discovery. We measure AB magnitudes of g=19.14 +/- 0.05, r=19.39 +/- 0.03, i=19.46 +/- 0.03, and z=19.53 +/- 0.09. These observations are consistent with the continuing rapid decline reported by ATLAS, while the blue colour (observed g-r = -0.26 +/- 0.06 mag) is also consistent with a possible foreground CV interpretation.
evidence_timeline.title: Kinder follow-up observations of AT 2026yos (ATLAS26jvy)

evidence_timeline.summary: Here we report the ATLAS discovery of the transient ATLAS26jvy (AT2026yos) in galaxy NGC6379 at AB magnitude, m_w = 18.53 +/- 0.04. At a distance of 87 Mpc, the transient was discovered on MJD 61262.93 (2026-08-10.93) with an absolute magnitude, M = -16.45 +/- 0.04. The last non-detection through forced photometry was on MJD 61261.97, when the transient possessed m_w > 21.4 (3-sigma). If associated with NGC6379, AT2026yos would possess a projected offset of 37.0 kpc. Further ATLAS observations indicate that AT2026yos has since faded at a rate of 0.33 mag/day. Given all of the above, we consider AT2026yos to be a plausible kilonova candidate, possessing an absolute magnitude, galaxy offset, and rise and fade rates consistent with those seen for previous events. As such, we strongly encourage spectroscopic classification.

publication_revisions.abstract: Here we report the ATLAS discovery of the transient ATLAS26jvy (AT2026yos) in galaxy NGC6379 at AB magnitude, m_w = 18.53 +/- 0.04. At a distance of 87 Mpc, the transient was discovered on MJD 61262.93 (2026-08-10.93) with an absolute magnitude, M = -16.45 +/- 0.04. The last non-detection through forced photometry was on MJD 61261.97, when the transient possessed m_w > 21.4 (3-sigma). If associated with NGC6379, AT2026yos would possess a projected offset of 37.0 kpc. Further ATLAS observations indicate that AT2026yos has since faded at a rate of 0.33 mag/day. Given all of the above, we consider AT2026yos to be a plausible kilonova candidate, possessing an absolute magnitude, galaxy offset, and rise and fade rates consistent with those seen for previous events. As such, we strongly encourage spectroscopic classification.
